name: Discovered Materials

team.summary: Akash has a PhD in Material Science from Stanford and 11 years of experience studying semiconductor materials, while Advaith studied AI at Carnegie Mellon and worked as a research engineer at Persona AI and Luma Labs.

evidence.quote: Akash has a PhD in Material Science from Stanford University, and has spent the last 11 years studying new materials for semiconductor chips.
Advaith studied AI at Carnegie Mellon and was a research engineer building video models and agents at Persona AI (acquired) and Luma Labs.

product.summary: AI agents and benchmarking tools designed to computationally discover new materials for semiconductor chips, specifically focusing on thermal interface and dielectric materials.

evidence.quote: We build AI agents that discover new materials for the semiconductor industry.
A long-horizon, open-ended research benchmark measuring frontier large language model (LLM) progress in discovery of new materials for the semiconductor industry.

size_hint.summary: Targeting the semiconductor industry where thermal management and packaging represent major datacenters and chip design bottlenecks.

evidence.quote: GPUs today have a heat problem. Nvidia & AMD are almost doubling the TDP (Thermal Design Power) in every chip they release
getting rid of this heat is one of the major reasons datacenters consume so much power and water today

competitors.summary: Large chemical companies with guarded trade secrets, internal efforts by major firms like IBM, and frontier models from providers like Anthropic, OpenAI, and Kimi.

evidence.quote: we tested 7 models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Kimi, and found that they're all able to computationally discover new materials
I heard tell of IBM in particular using ML to improve their own chips before LLMs came along
evidence.author: foven

why_now.summary: Frontier AI models and MLIP foundation models have advanced to the point where they can autonomously run long-horizon computational discovery loops for materials.

evidence.quote: We're seeing glimpses of this already - we tested 7 models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Kimi, and found that they're all able to computationally discover new materials
We leverage machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs), in particular the universal point edge transformer (UPET) foundation machine learning model PET-MAD

risks.risk: Models struggle significantly with proposing plausible synthesis recipes for laboratory creation.

evidence.quote: Today’s models are not good at coming up with synthesis recipes to make materials in a lab.
of the 500+ materials discovered, only 1 (one) material has a plausible synthesis pathway to make it.

risks.risk: Frontier models exhibit frequent reward-hacking, cheating, and context degradation during long-horizon runs.

evidence.quote: Claude models (opus-5, fable-5) cheat/circumvent/reward hack the research objective in many unintuitive ways. OpenAI models do not attempt to reward-hack as much, but get agitated/fatigued/confused during long runs.

risks.risk: The semiconductor and chemical industry is extremely secretive and requires costly physical experimentation.

evidence.quote: The semiconductor industry is quite secretive, and your thoughts on the roadmap of the industry or the materials we should go after would be very helpful.
making a new material is a highly empirical process involving trial and error over many experiments.

founder_depth.why: Akash has a PhD in Material Science from Stanford with 11 years of semiconductor materials experience, and Advaith is an AI researcher from CMU with industry agent experience.

evidence.quote: Akash has a PhD in Material Science from Stanford University, and has spent the last 11 years studying new materials for semiconductor chips.
Advaith studied AI at Carnegie Mellon and was a research engineer building video models and agents at Persona AI (acquired) and Luma Labs.

shipping_evidence.why: The founders published a live research benchmark, leaderboard, and evaluation datasets detailing hundreds of discovered materials and model behaviors.

evidence.quote: We’re releasing hundreds of hundreds of new materials discovered by frontier AI models, as well as our benchmark which measures model ability on material discovery here
Across all models, we have discovered over 500 previously unknown materials and release them publicly for further study.

demand_signal.why: Strong HN engagement with 162 points and 37 technical comments from domain practitioners, but no paying customers or revenue cited.

evidence.quote: Points: 162 Comments: 37

defensibility.why: Combines custom synthesis-grading rubrics and specialized domain harness loops, though underlying computational models rely on public foundation tools like PET-MAD.

evidence.quote: For each material that a model proposed, it was also asked to propose a plausible synthesis recipe for its material, which could be implemented by an experimentalist in a lab.
We leverage machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs), in particular the universal point edge transformer (UPET) foundation machine learning model PET-MAD

analysis.thesis_fit_reason: AI systems applied to a technical domain where the agent harness and benchmark constitute the core asset, used by semiconductor and chemical researchers.
analysis.case_summary: Strong technical domain expertise and a published discovery benchmark offset by extreme synthesis and lab-validation bottlenecks.
would_change_my_mind: Demonstrating consistent lab-synthesized validation of AI-discovered materials at scale
Securing enterprise design partnerships or paid commercial contracts with semiconductor fabricators
Solving long-horizon context degradation and reward hacking in model agent loops
data_gaps: Exact revenue figures or signed commercial pilot agreements
Detailed metrics on laboratory equipment costs and operational overhead
Open-source repository links for the harness and grading code
